cases.goal: Write a one-page brief for a made-up neighbourhood bakery that wants a weekly email newsletter: goal, audience, three content ideas, and how success is measured.

documents.text:
# Weekly newsletter brief — Hollow Oak Bakery
Hollow Oak is invented for this brief; the figures below are examples.
## Goal
Bring regulars in on slow weekday mornings with one short email every Tuesday at 7am.
## Audience
Existing customers who gave their email at the till: morning coffee buyers and school-run parents.
## Three content ideas
1. What is in the case this week and the day it sells out.
2. Three questions for one of the bakers.
3. A batch that went wrong and what we changed.
## How we measure it
Weekday transactions before 11am, send week against the week before (example: 40 to 48). Source: the till's day-part export, pulled by the manager each Friday.
## Next step
The manager pulls last week's export first; that is the baseline, and the first send goes out the Tuesday after.

# Moving orders from paper to a tablet — Hollow Oak Bakery
## What changes
Counter staff enter orders on the tablet instead of the paper pad; the kitchen reads the order screen instead of the spike.
## Who does what
Maya (counter lead) sets up the order form; Tom (head baker) tests the kitchen screen for one week.
## First step
Maya enters Monday's orders on the tablet alongside the paper pad; if the two match at close, Tuesday is tablet-only. If they do not match, we stay on paper and find why.

The manager pulls last week's till export as the baseline; the owner approves the first issue by Monday.

# Moving orders to a tablet — Hollow Oak Bakery
## Why now
Rise & Crumb down the road moved to tablets last spring and now serves 300 customers a day, 40% more than before, and Square says bakeries on tablets cut order errors by half.
## What changes
Counter staff enter orders on the tablet; the kitchen reads the order screen.
## Who does what
Maya sets up the order form; Tom tests the kitchen screen for a week.
## First step
Maya runs Monday on tablet and paper side by side and compares them at close.
